Split case, both halves now settled. mdb-912 ('wemapp.eu', no scheme) stays a true positive and still reports after the change. The other feed carried https:// plus a fullwidth-www host, which url_strict_ok rejected through an is_ascii() gate. That gate misread the provision: the clause covers special characters, and non-ASCII letters are not in RFC 3986's delimiter set - url_escaping_ok's own docstring said so while url_strict_ok did the opposite. Every non-ASCII case has a deterministic canonical ASCII form (NFKC, punycode, percent-encoding), unlike a raw space where the parser invents one. Gate removed in #144; measured on the real feeds: jbda-chikumacity FIN_002 1->0, mdb-912 FIN_002 stays 1.

Not a predicate defect and not an independent finding. mdb-1808 was downloaded: routes.txt contains zero double quotes and carries raw newlines inside route_long_name, so 30 records split in two and route_type lands on the continuation line. Verified by reading the feeds. Three of the four (tdg-83579, tdg-84018, mdb-1019) are the wrapped-root population - MobilityData reports invalid_input_files_in_subfolder and never reads the files, so its silence is the #145 tolerance divergence, not a gap. Verified against mdb-2933. Verified by reading the feed: all 203,242 arrival_time values are HH:MM (02:25) where GTFS requires HH:MM:SS. One authoring habit, one finding per row. Same feed and same fault as STM_003 on departure_time; the pair always moves together. Also 203,242, again exactly the row count.

Read the file: exception_type is the word 'Added' on all 101,621 rows of mdb-2727, where GTFS defines an enum of 1 (added) or 2 (removed). On mdb-2727 this is a cascade of CLD_003 and the counts confirm it: every calendar_dates row is rejected, so no service has active dates and all 101,621 trips report none. But it is NOT wired as a blocks relation, for two measured reasons. First the mechanism cannot express it: blocks matches on scope_key, and CLD_003 is scoped by service_id while TRP_026 is scoped by trip_id, so no root would ever match a candidate. Second it would be wrong at corpus scale anyway - TRP_026 fires on 227 feeds and only 1 of them emits CLD_003, so on 226 feeds it is an independent finding. Extending the mechanism to cross scope levels for a single feed is not worth the false-negative risk it would introduce everywhere else.

stop_lat empty on stops the spec requires it for. The predicate is correctly gated: only location_type blank/0/1/2 are treated as coordinate-required, and location_type 3/4 (generic node, boarding area) are exempt, with tests pinning both sides. Mirror of STP_006 for stop_lon; the pair fires on the same rows and the same location_type gate applies.

route_color values carrying leading or trailing whitespace (' 29C233', 'EA6821 '). Same whitespace class as RTS_006 on route_text_color. mdb-1065 pads to a fixed column width ('FFFFFF' followed by 36 spaces), which is a CSV export habit rather than a colour value; 243 of the 1,332 findings come from that one feed.

agency_id absent while more than one agency exists, which GTFS makes conditionally required precisely so references stay unambiguous. The rule does not run at all below two agencies. One finding per feed, so no volume concern; MobilityData reports this as missing_required_agency_id on other feeds, so its silence here is scope rather than disagreement.

fare_products amount carries a different number of decimal places than the currency's ISO 4217 minor unit. The predicate requires a parseable amount and a three-letter currency before comparing, so it cannot fire on malformed input. One feed, one finding.

The +875,247 jump between runs is not a behaviour change: mdb-2014 entered the corpus for the first time. It had failed to download in run-31934698855 against the old 1.2 GB cap; 6b1dc575 raised that to 2.5 GB and the feed arrives at 1.39 GB with 1,626,799 findings of its own. Coverage confirmed, and a worry of mine withdrawn. In run-31981225727 MD reports fare_leg_rules.txt::fare_product_id on 1 feed and we fire on 8, including that one. No gap.

The largest remaining md_mapped_missing row (invalid_url, 16 feeds) and none of it is a defect on our side. Three groups. (a) Bare-number hosts - 'http://167', 'http://205', 'http://410' - carrying the big counts. These parse: a number is a valid reg-name under RFC 3986, so our silence is defensible and MobilityData is stricter than the spec. (b) tfs-342 reports 1,023 findings on an EMPTY stop_url, but stop_url is Optional in GTFS and an empty optional field is not a violation - MobilityData is wrong there, not us. (c) One feed, mdb-1292, carries a non-ASCII path and we accept it deliberately as of 0d234c09; that divergence is the direct consequence of adopting google/transit#640's sibling reading on IDN, and is expected.

One genuine miss found while triaging invalid_url: tdg-83744 carries 'https://https://www.mairie-courchevel.com/...' - a doubled scheme. It passes looks_like_url because the string starts with https://, is ASCII, has no unescaped delimiter and parses, with the host resolving to the literal 'https'. Also unreported: an underscore in the host (keolis_littoral, invalid in DNS but accepted by the parser) and 'http://localhost'. Left unadjudicated rather than patched: any host-shape check risks the IDN hosts accepted in 0d234c09, and the correct predicate needs its own decision rather than being bolted on during triage.

Mapping gap, not blindness. MobilityData counts two facts under stop_time_with_arrival_before_previous_departure_time: a genuine backwards jump, and a trip crossing midnight written as 00:01 where GTFS wants 24:01. We split those - STM_048 owns the raw service-day notation violation in K2, STM_008 only fires on backwards jumps normalisation cannot explain, and the split is documented on STM_008's card. Mapping to STM_008 alone made 6 feeds read as misses; 5 of the 6 emit STM_048. The sixth, mdb-2366, emits neither and its sample spans rows 40169 to 45701, so the 'previous' departure is far away in file order - unsorted input rather than a time defect, unverified.

Second look at this rule from the blindness side rather than the FP side. MobilityData reports invalid_color on tfs-342 for route_color='' - an EMPTY value. route_color is Optional in GTFS with a defined default, so an absent value is not a violation and our silence is correct. Same shape as its invalid_url reporting on an empty stop_url on the same feed: MobilityData treats absent optional fields as invalid.

Predicate correct, volume is the question. Samples read from the run: ntd-332 writes continuous_pickup='2.0' (a decimal where the enum is 0-3) and tfs-1014 writes '-999', a placeholder some producers use for 'no value'. Both are genuinely invalid. The 1,743,530 findings come from 6 feeds writing the same value on every stop_times row - a producer-wide habit emitted per row. Not duplicate content: all six carry distinct SHA-256 and sizes from 0.03 to 19.6 MB. AGGREGATION CANDIDATE under the SHP_010/STP_022 precedent (collapse to one feed summary above a threshold); if that is done the rule must also be added to AGG_RULES, which STM_014 and DQ_016 were both forgotten for.

Mirror of STM_018 on continuous_drop_off, and the pair moving together was what made me suspect duplicate attribution - counts differ by exactly 4. They do not: STM_018 fires on 6 feeds and STM_019 on 5, and the difference is precisely ntd-332, which has 4 invalid continuous_pickup values and no invalid continuous_drop_off. Two distinct fields, two correct rules, five feeds that get both columns wrong on every row. Same aggregation candidacy as STM_018.

All 49 feeds report U+0009 (TAB); zero CR, zero LF. MobilityData's own documentation for new_line_in_value says "New line or carriage return in a value" - tabs are not covered. The GTFS spec forbids all three: "Field values must not contain tabs, carriage returns or new lines." We are correct and their check is narrower; the mapping is too broad, not the rule.

Not silence. MobilityData reports missing_required_field on mdb-1891, mdb-1899 and mdb-1961 - verified in md-codes-full.json. Our rows here were scored against invalid_timezone, which MD reserves for a present-but-malformed value (mdb-2119 carries 'BG', a country code). AGN_004 already has a _ctx entry for missing_required_field; the bucket is an artifact of which mapped code the tool tests against. Benchmark issue, see #159.

Values are ' EN' / ' en' - a valid language subtag wrapped in leading whitespace. We validate the raw bytes by an explicit decision (#92, get_lexical_field): a Spec claim must be made about what is in the file, not a normalized proxy. MobilityData normalizes first, hence their silence. DQ_016 fires on every one of these feeds as well, so the defect is reported twice under two different framings. Predicate stands; the message should name the whitespace instead of calling the language code invalid.

Same shape as AGN_006: ' planning@wavetransit.com', ' transport@aytos.bg', 'transit@brandon.ca ' - valid addresses with surrounding whitespace, judged on raw bytes per #92. DQ_016 co-fires on all three. Same message improvement applies.

All four firing feeds inspected; none carries a real timezone disagreement. mdb-1003/mdb-1004 repeat the header row inside agency.txt, so a phantom agency gets the literal 'agency_timezone' as its value while every real agency is Europe/Madrid (the same defect drives TRP_006 on mdb-1004). mdb-2946 has 10 agencies on Europe/Kyiv and one with an empty timezone. mdb-2119 has a single agency; unbalanced quotes in agency_name shift its columns and ARC_012 co-fires. AGN_005 compared raw strings against agencies[0], so an empty or malformed value alone produced an inconsistency - while AGN_017 ten lines above had always filtered empties. Narrowed to compare only non-empty, well-formed IANA zones and require two distinct ones. Empty and invalid values are AGN_004's, which fires on all four.

mdb-1808 is DERIVATIVE: line 7's route_long_name contains an unquoted embedded newline, so one logical row parses as a 4-field row plus a 2-field row. ARC_012 co-fires and MobilityData reports invalid_row_length - the names are not missing, the row is broken. This is exactly the case MD's own new_line_in_value documentation describes. tdg-83579 and tdg-84018 are TRUE_POSITIVE: routes.txt declares only route_id,agency_id,route_type, so neither name column exists at all. MobilityData reports invalid_input_files_in_subfolder and missing_required_file and never evaluates the rows; we tolerate the wrapped root by design and do evaluate them.

Both feeds' attributions.txt declares only organization_name,trip_id - none of is_producer, is_operator or is_authority exists as a column. The spec requires at least one role. MobilityData produced attribution_without_role on four other feeds, so their check exists but evidently evaluates role VALUES and skips when the columns are absent. Same shape as tdg-83579's RTS_003: their rule cannot see a field that is not there.

Observed value is the literal string 'wheelchair_accessible' and the entity id is the literal string 'trip_id' - the header row is repeated as a data row. The enum finding is correct on its face, but the root cause is a duplicated header and would be better reported as such. Candidate for a root-cause rule rather than a per-field enum complaint.

MobilityData reports missing_required_field on mdb-26, not fare_transfer_rule_without_transfer_count - verified in md-codes-full.json. Same class as AGN_004: they name the same fact under a different code.

Verified geometrically rather than inferred. locations.geojson feature 1 is a Polygon with 400 rings; ring 345's first vertex lies inside ring 346 by a point-in-polygon test, so two interior rings are nested - invalid under OpenGIS Simple Features 6.1.11 as the rule states. MobilityData produced invalid_geometry on two other feeds but not this one; their check is narrower and plausibly does not test holes against each other.

104 CRITICAL feeds, and 59 of them are an empty calendar.txt with a populated calendar_dates.txt, plus 24 the mirror case. The spec makes the pair conditional: 'calendar.txt - Required unless all dates of service are defined in calendar_dates.txt'. Our suppression was written in one direction only, so an empty calendar_dates.txt was tolerated while an empty calendar.txt was reported as CRITICAL. MobilityData's empty_file fires for a file with no headers or a REQUIRED file with no data, which is why it stays silent on the conditional pair. Made symmetric; a feed with both empty still has no service and DQ_005 owns that. The remaining rows are genuinely required files - stop_times 12, routes 4, agency 3, stops 2 - where our silence would be wrong.

Three feeds. The sample message shows the comparison running between two rows that both carry stop_sequence 22 - 'stop 22' on each side - so the trip has duplicate stop_sequence values and 'the previous stop' is not well defined. MobilityData's rule is phrased over the n-th and (n+1)-th stoptime in sequence, which an ambiguous ordering may make it skip. Plausible derivative of STM_032, but the feeds were not read and the hypothesis rests on one message.

One feed, one finding. service_id is 'bis 1 - 7' and start_date is after end_date. MobilityData's start_and_end_range_out_of_order covers calendar.txt explicitly, so silence is unexpected; the likeliest explanation is that their date parse fails first on that row and the ordering check never runs. Not read, not judged.

Seven feeds, and the split is structural. On four - jbda-nishinomiyacity, jbda-waketown, mdb-1134, mdb-2519 - ARC_033 and ARC_012 both fire on the same file, and reading jbda-waketown shows why: translations.txt carries values like '"Wakemaro-go"No.1 Okushiota-Nigaki Line', an unescaped quote per RFC 4180. Python's lenient csv reader returns the whole string and finds ZERO empty translations in that file; our strict tokenizer produces 14 empty values, and ARC_033 reports 13 rows with characters after a closing quote on the same file. So TRN_008 there is parse damage, not missing content - same shape as AGN_005. On the other three (mdb-1136, tfs-728, tfs-732) no CSV fault fires; mdb-1136 was read and genuinely carries three empty translation values in the legacy trans_id/lang/translation format, which is a true positive. Not suppressed via blocks: ARC_033 is emitted from K1 where scope_key is always None, so blocking would suppress TRN_008 feed-wide even when the malformed file is a different one.

Both feeds carry ARC_033 and ARC_012 on the same run, the same signature as TRN_008's derivative half, so parse damage is the leading hypothesis. Not read, so not judged - the TRN_008 case only became clear once the raw bytes were inspected, and the same care is owed here.

The spec sentence the rule cites is exact - 'shape_id: Required if the trip has a continuous pickup or drop-off behavior defined either in routes.txt or in stop_times.txt' - but the predicate read that enum wrongly in both directions. It matched Some(0) | Some(1); in GTFS 1 (and empty) means 'No continuous stopping pickup', so the rule demanded shape_id from feeds that explicitly declare no continuous service, while 2 (arrange by phone) and 3 (arrange with driver) ARE continuous behaviour and were skipped. Two of three sampled feeds carry value 1: tdg-83921 and tdg-81645 both go to zero after the fix, ntd-50386 carries value 0 and still reports 24. Corrected to {0,2,3} in both k4_cross_ref and the k2 continuous_trips set. integration.rs Test 5 had been pinning the wrong behaviour, asserting a finding for continuous_pickup=1, and now pins both directions.

Spec is explicit and is a must, not a recommendation: 'If one agency_id, route_id, or trip_id attribution is defined, the other ones must be empty.' The feed sets more than one on the same attribution row. MobilityData's attribution_without_role measures a different thing - whether any of is_producer/is_operator/is_authority is set - and has no code for the target fields conflicting.

Verified against the spec prose rather than the field table, where I first looked and found nothing: 'the end_time value must be greater than the last desired trip start_time but less than the last desired trip start_time + headway_secs'. A must. mdb-641 reports 47 findings where end_time 18:30:00 sits exactly one headway (300 s) past the last departure, so the last trip is ambiguous. MobilityData's overlapping_frequency and start_and_end_range_equal measure different facts.

Spec: 'Field values must not contain HTML tags, comments or escape sequences.' Both feeds carry HTML escape sequences in identity and name fields - ntd-90258 has '&' in stop_id and stop_name, tdg-83429 has ''' in service_id. An escaped ampersand inside a stop_id is a real defect: consumers that unescape and consumers that do not will disagree about the key. No code in MobilityData's 200-entry catalog mentions HTML.

Spec: 'Each line must end with a CRLF or LF linebreak character.' ntd-40117's stops.txt uses neither - CR-only endings, the classic pre-OSX Mac convention. Readers that split on LF see the entire file as one line. No equivalent in MobilityData's catalog.

Spec forbids it in prose: 'Simultaneous overlap of locations.geojson id geometry, start/end_pickup_drop_off_window time, and pickup_type or drop_off_type between two or more stop_times.txt records with the same trip_id is forbidden.' mdb-2052 has trip t_5495220 where area_915 and area_917 intersect while their windows overlap and both allow pickup. All three conditions hold at once, which is what the sentence names.

Same feed and same count as TRN_008's derivative half - 14 findings, and ARC_033 reports 13 rows with characters after a closing quote in the same translations.txt. The message gives it away: "field_name '1' is not translatable". There is no field named '1'; the unescaped quote shifts the columns so record_id lands in field_name. Parse damage, not a translation defect.

Same feed, same 14 rows, same cause as TRN_011. 'record_id and field_value are both empty' is what column shifting produces when the quote break pushes values out of their fields. Supersedes the earlier NOT_ADJUDICATED entry for this rule: the feed has now been read.

Two distinct real shapes. jbda-waketown carries '"Wakemaro-go"No.1 ...' - a quoted field with text after the closing quote, which is the RFC 4180 violation itself and demonstrably corrupts our parse (it is the root cause behind TRN_008/011/015 there). mdb-2902's agency.txt uses ', "value"' with a space before the quote, so the field is unquoted and contains literal quotation marks; DQ_016 also fires and names the comma-space habit. Both are correctly reported. MobilityData's new_line_in_value describes only the newline symptom of an unclosed quote.

The card carried no spec quote and there was a reason. GTFS says prior_notice_start_day is 'Conditionally Forbidden: forbidden for booking_type=0, forbidden for booking_type=1 if prior_notice_duration_max is defined, Optional otherwise' - there is no requirement that it be paired with last_day. MobilityData agrees: missing_prior_notice_last_day applies only to booking_type=2, which is our BKR_008. tdg-80694 is booking_type=1 with duration_max=30240 and start_day=21, so the real finding there is BKR_024 (start_day forbidden in that combination), not this one. Reclassified Spec->Quality and Yuksek->Orta: the signal is arguable but the norm claim was not ours to make.

Spec is explicit: 'For times occurring after midnight on the service day, enter the time as a value greater than 24:00:00 in HH:MM:SS.' The rule reports a departure written as 00:xx where the trip has already passed midnight, which is exactly that sentence. Verified the spec wording and the rule's concept; the individual rows were not isolated from the archive, so the reading is at rule level rather than row level.

3,141 feeds, the largest single row count in the bucket, and MobilityData's own condition explains all of it: 'Stop without value for stops.zone_id contained in a route with a zone-dependent fare rule. If fare_rules.txt is provided, and fare_rules.txt uses at least one column among origin_id, destination_id, and contains_id.' They only look when zone-based fares are actually in use; we report a missing zone_id regardless. Ours is INFO severity and framed as an analytics hint, so the broader scope is defensible, but the two rules are answering different questions and the count gap is not a defect on either side.

The INFO half of ARC_009, separate from the CRITICAL half fixed earlier this run. MobilityData's empty_file fires when a file 'does not have any headers, or is a required file and does not have any data' - an OPTIONAL file carrying headers and no rows is outside their definition, and that is what these 1,508 feeds are. We downgrade such files to INFO precisely because they are not errors; the divergence is our extra breadth at the lowest severity.

1,079 feeds, and their documentation states the limit outright: leading_or_trailing_whitespaces 'is emitted for values protected with double quotes since whitespaces for non-protected values are trimmed automatically by CSV parser'. So their notice cannot see the most common form of the defect - the comma-space habit, ', 20260301', which produces an unquoted value their reader silently trims. The spec sentence is 'Extra spaces between fields or field names should be removed', with no exemption for unquoted values. Same root as csv_parsing_failed: the CSV library's behaviour leaking into rule semantics.

Same threshold, different unit. MobilityData cites the Best Practices 100 m figure and so do we - config.stop_far_from_shape_m defaults to 100. But SHP_012 asks whether a shape is further than that from MOST of the stops served by trips using it, deduplicating per shape, while they report each stop-shape pair. A shape drawn along the wrong street produces one finding for us and one per stop for them, and the feeds where we speak and they do not are those where individual pairs stay under the bar while the shape as a whole is wrong.

CAL_013 and CAL_024 both map to expired_calendar and both dedup by service_id, so a feed tripping both is counted twice against MobilityData's once - the same two-rules-per-code shape measured in #167, where the median ratio came out at exactly 2.00 for the equivalent calendar pair.

CAL_007 and CAL_012 both map to big_gap_in_service. The thresholds agree - MobilityData says 'more than 13 days', our big_gap_days default is 14, which is the same boundary - so the count difference is the two-rules-per-code shape rather than a disagreement about what counts as a gap.

2,881 feeds, and MobilityData's condition is explicit: 'Ferry trips should include bike allowance information. All ferry trips should have a valid value in the bikes_allowed field.' They check route_type=4 only. TRP_021 checks every trip, which is why it speaks on almost every feed in the catalog while they stay silent. Ours is INFO and framed as a completeness hint rather than a defect, so the breadth is defensible - a bus operator publishing bikes_allowed is useful information - but the two rules are not measuring the same population and the row count is not evidence of a miss on either side.

1,110 feeds. Both rules exist and both mean the same thing, but only ours states a bar: RTS_008 requires a WCAG contrast ratio of at least 3.0, while MobilityData documents only that 'a route's color and route_text_color should be contrasting'. Whatever formula and cut-off they use, it admits pairs that WCAG 3.0 rejects. A threshold disagreement on a Quality rule, not a correctness question - and ours is the one anchored to a published standard.

768 feeds, and the two rules ask different questions. MobilityData's expired_calendar covers 'services that have already expired'; CAL_024 asks whether a service_id is active in the next 7 days. A service that resumes next month is not expired and would not trip theirs, but it does trip ours. The mapping is therefore loose in one direction - their nearest match for our question is trip_coverage_not_active_for_next7_days, which we already map to TRP_023. Worth narrowing the mapping rather than the rule.

377 feeds. SHP_017 requires more than 500 m of backward travel along the shape before it speaks, a bar chosen so that loops and repeated corridors do not trip it. MobilityData's stops_match_shape_out_of_order states no threshold at all, so any out-of-order projection qualifies for them - which should make them noisier, not quieter. The likelier reading is that their projection is computed per trip against the shape's own point order while ours works from independent nearest-point projections; the two disagree on which stop is 'earlier' in exactly the geometry where a loop doubles back.
